claims.read: Every public interface member across the three environments is one word: `RecorderInterface` (calls, count, handler, clear), `SignalInterface` (controller, signal, count), `ResourceFactoryInterface` (created, destroyed, create, destroy), `TeardownInterface` (count, add, destroy), `EventSourceInterface` (on), `ScratchInterface` (path, write, read, has, names, ensure, link, remove, destroy), `ScratchIdentity` (device, inode, birth), `LoopbackInterface` (url, port, destroy), `CookieJarInterface` (header, read, capture), `PortfolioInterface` (variant, placements, paths, files, place), `JournalInterface` (steps, output, start, stop, record), `JournalStep` (action, trigger, result). Every option key is one word too: `WaitOptions` (budget, interval, signal), `RetryOptions` (attempts), `ScratchOptions` (parent, prefix, files), `InventoryOptions` (extensions, exclude), `UpgradeOptions` (path, protocols), `ElementOptions` (classes, text, attributes), `FrameOptions` (path, width, height, element), `PortfolioOptions` (states, variants, variant, directory, enabled), `CaptureVariant` (name, width, height, apply). I attacked the overload families against `.claude/rules/names.md` § Split behavioral variants: `resolveAccessible`, `clickAccessible`, `readRing`, and `readContrast` each keep one algorithm and take an extra datum, so none is a magic mode. `render` is the one shape where the first parameter's meaning changes with arity and the shape of work changes with it; the guide rules that shape deliberately, so it is recorded as test-subj-12 with verdict EXEMPT rather than as a violation. I attacked `CookieJarInterface` as an unnamed manager owing `cookie(name)`/`cookies()` under `.claude/rules/patterns.md` § Managers and rejected the reading: the jar exposes no item collection, its verbs are `read`/`capture`, and `read` is the same term `ScratchInterface` uses for the same concept. No `*Manager` type exists, so the batch-overload family has no subject here. I attacked `PortfolioInterface.files` against `.paths` as synonym-for-two-concepts and `PortfolioOptions.variant` against `.variants`; neither has a rule sentence that fires, and both repairs rename published members, so I do not raise them.

claims.claim: S2 Vocabulary and forms — helper prefixes carry their one project-wide meaning; the identifier tables hold; `is*`/`parse*`/`create*`/`*Of`/`{noun}To{Noun}` keep their contracts; lifecycle verbs keep their fixed meanings; tallies follow § Tallies; acronyms keep canonical case; no rejected name; booleans read as assertions; discriminants name their axis; a binary switch is a boolean; one term per concept.
claims.read: Read every exported identifier in `src/core`, `src/server`, and `src/browser` against `.claude/rules/names.md`. Acronyms keep canonical case throughout: `decodeJSONLines`, `roundTripJSON`, `JSONValue`, `JSONSafe`, `parseCSSColor`, `IMPLICIT_ROLES`. Type-level forms hold: `{Entity}Interface`, `{Entity}Options`, `{Entity}Result` (`UpgradeResult`), `{Entity}Handler` (`TeardownHandler`), `{Entity}EventMap` (none needed), no `I` prefix, no pluralized type name. `is*` guards are total and return false off-shape (`isRecorderMapComplete` wraps its whole body in try/catch; `isRendered`, `isReachable`, `isOutsideViewport`, `isExcluded`, `isRunning` throw nothing). `parse*` returns `T | undefined` (`parseColor`, `parseCSSColor`). `create*` in `factories.ts` all construct. Booleans read as assertions (`enabled`, `claimed`, `aborted`). Discriminants name their axis: `claimed` on `UpgradeResult`, `success` on `Result`; neither is `kind` or `type`. Binary switches are booleans (`PortfolioOptions.enabled`, `claimed`), never two-literal unions. `count` is the lone tally on each entity that has one, so § Tallies' ambiguity ban does not fire. Grepped for the rejected words `data`, `info`, `item`, `kind`, `cfg`, `msg`, `obj`, `thing` as members: the only hits are `createChannel`'s `...data` rest parameter and the `info` key in the intercepted console record, both transliterating `lib.dom`'s own `Console` signature, which the TSDoc names as the source it mirrors, so § General vocabulary's mirrored-name allowance covers them. I attacked the `resolve*` prefix against § Standalone helpers' 'picks the effective value from options and defaults' for `resolveRoot`, `resolveContained`, `resolveRendered`, and `resolveAccessible`, then probed the fleet (`export function resolve[A-Z]` across every package's `src/**`): `resolvePath`, `resolveLink`, `resolveURL`, `resolveExecutable`, and `resolveWorkspaceFile` use the same broader sense, so this is a fleet-wide convention rather than a package defect and I struck the finding. I attacked `checkBounds` against `requireValue`/`requireContained` as two prefixes for one concept and struck it: `require*` returns the value it narrowed and `check*` returns void, which is a real distinction the package holds to consistently.

claims.claim: S3 Options and emitters — options are single-word keys grouped by entity noun with `on` reserved for hooks; a stateful entity owns an `Emitter` by composition with the seven-step pattern and a focused event map of present-tense verbs or nouns, no `status` event, errors typed `unknown`.
claims.read: Read every options interface in `src/core/types.ts`, `src/server/types.ts`, and `src/browser/types.ts` against `.claude/rules/patterns.md` § Options: every top-level key is one word, no key encodes grouping through a prefix (`ScratchOptions.parent`/`prefix`, not `scratchParent`), and no options object uses `on`, so the § Options reservation is intact. `EventSourceInterface.on` is an interface method mirroring an emitter's own subscribe method rather than an option key, so the reservation does not reach it. I attacked § Stateful emitters against `JournalInterface` (start/stop/record are lifecycle transitions) and `PortfolioInterface` (place is an observable operation) and rejected the reading on two grounds: neither entity publishes anything a consumer subscribes to — a journal is read after the fact through `steps` and `output` snapshots, and a portfolio is read through `placements` and `paths` — and the pattern's `Emitter`, `EmitterHooks`, and `EmitterErrorHandler` all originate in `@orkestrel/emitter`, which this package deliberately does not declare (guides/test.md:998-1000, README.md:15-17). No local emitter, no `status` event, and no domain event map exists to check.

claims.claim: S4 Design laws — state is derived rather than stored twice; literal unions represent real domain states only; no compatibility shim; mechanism not product policy; no polling architecture; the public API is minimal and every intentional capability is exposed.
claims.read: Derived state holds everywhere I could attack it: `RecorderInterface.count` is a getter over `calls.length` (src/core/factories.ts:132-134), `TeardownInterface.count` over `handlers.length` (309-314), `SignalInterface.count` over `registrations.length` (276-278), `ResourceFactoryInterface.create` numbers from `created.calls.length + 1` (293-297), and `createJournal` uses the presence of `intercepted` as the started flag with a comment stating that no second flag can disagree with it (src/browser/factories.ts:210-213). No literal union is decorative: `UpgradeResult` and `Result` both discriminate on a boolean, which is what `AGENTS.md` § Design laws requires of a binary switch. No compatibility alias, deprecation shim, or re-export of another package's symbol exists — `src/core/index.ts`, `src/server/index.ts`, and `src/browser/index.ts` hold only `export * from` rows. Mechanism-not-policy holds and is argued at length in the guide's Limits table, which refuses a hostile-key table, a numeric corpus, a surface digest, and a control extractor precisely as one suite's policy. Two design-law tensions are real and both are licensed in writing, so they are recorded as test-subj-13 and test-subj-14 with verdict EXEMPT: the wait family's polling, and `readPixels` returning `0` where the resolved value carries no number. On minimal API I attacked `dropRegistration`, which the guide itself admits no consumer can reach (guides/test.md:168-171), and struck it: `.claude/rules/architecture.md` § Declaration placement requires every declaration in a centralized file to be exported, and § Barrel exports forbids gating exposure on consumer count, so its exposure is mandated and the guide's honesty about the limitation is the right shape.
